article.html.text:
HomeAbout
Choosing a grid for editorial work
Editorial layout lives and dies by its grid. This article walks through
choosing column counts, setting a baseline rhythm, and knowing when to break
the grid on purpose for a feature spread.
A twelve-column grid gives the most flexibility for magazines: two text
columns with wide margins, or a full-bleed image when the story demands it.
The baseline grid keeps captions and pull quotes aligned with body text
without extra work.
Break the grid rarely. A single element that ignores the columns reads as
deliberate; two or more read as mistakes. Save rule-breaking for the opening
spread and let the rest of the article settle into rhythm.
